item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
343
ABPZ20 KNHC 252327
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Sat Jul 25 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Fausto, located well east of the Hawaiian Islands, and on Tropical
Storm Genevieve, located well south-southwest of the southwestern
coast of Mexico.

Well Southwest of Hawaii (CP92):
A large area of disorganized showers and thunderstorms located well
southwest of the Hawaiian Islands is associated with a broad area of
low pressure. Environmental conditions appear conducive for gradual
development of this system while it moves generally westward at
about 10 mph toward the International Date Line, and a tropical
depression is likely to form in the western Pacific basin early next
week.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...50 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...80 percent.

&&

Products issued by the U.S. Joint Typhoon Warning Center can be
found at: www.metoc.navy.mil/jtwc/jtwc.html

Official tropical cyclone forecast information issued by the Japan
Meteorological Agency for the western Pacific basin can be found at:
www.jma.go.jp/jma/jma-eng/jma-center/rsmc-hp-pub-eg/RSMC_HP.html

$$
Forecaster Gibbs/Evans/Pierce

Hurricane Fausto Advisory Number  29
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP062026
500 PM HST Sat Jul 25 2026
 
...FAUSTO HOLDING STEADY...
...EXPECTED TO MOVE INTO THE CENTRAL PACIFIC EARLY SUNDAY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 PM HST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.5N 138.8W
ABOUT 1060 MI...1705 KM E OF HILO HAWAII
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...100 MPH...155 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 280 DEGREES AT 13 MPH...20 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...971 MB...28.68 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests in the Hawaiian Islands should monitor the progress of
Fausto.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 PM HST (0300 UTC), the center of Hurricane Fausto was located
near latitude 19.5 North, longitude 138.8 West. Fausto is moving
toward the west near 13 mph (20 km/h), and this general
motion is expected to continue for the next several days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 100 mph (155 km/h) with higher
gusts. Gradual weakening is forecast during the next several days.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 50 miles (85 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 185 miles
(295 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 971 mb (28.68 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Fausto can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP1 and WMO header WTPZ41 KNHC.
 
SURF: Surf generated by Fausto is expected to begin building across
east-facing shores of the eastern end of Hawaii on Sunday, spreading
westward Sunday night into Monday, and continue building through
Tuesday as Fausto approaches and moves into the area. These
swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions. Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 PM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Gibbs/Evans/Pierce

item.title: Hurricane Fausto Forecast Discussion Number 29
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Sat Jul 25 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 260236
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Fausto Discussion Number  29
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP062026
500 PM HST Sat Jul 25 2026
 
Satellite imagery indicates that Fausto's overall structure has 
changed little during the past several hours. Despite the dry 
surrounding environment and the occasional dry air intrusion, the 
cyclone has maintained its convective structure with a symmetric 
eyewall and well-established outflow. The ragged eye, however, has 
recently become obscured with clouds. The latest subjective Dvorak 
intensity estimate from TAFB is T5.0/90 kt, while objective 
intensity estimates from UW-CIMSS range from 80 to around 95 kt. 
Based on the satellite presentation and a blend of the available 
intensity estimates, the initial intensity is held at 85 kt.

The initial motion is estimated to be 280/11 kt, and this general 
motion is expected to continue through the next several days as a 
strong subtropical ridge remains positioned north of the cyclone. 
The latest track guidance has come into better agreement and remains 
tightly clustered through the middle portion of next week as the 
system passes north of the Hawaiian Islands. The NHC forecast has 
again been nudged slightly northward toward the multi-model 
consensus (HCCA) between 60-96 h. 
 
Fausto is moving into a drier mid-level environment over marginal 
sea-surface temperatures, and southwesterly vertical wind shear is 
expected to increase after 36 h while the system moves over the 
central Pacific basin. Simulated satellite imagery depicts a similar 
evolution, maintaining a well-defined cyclone into tomorrow before 
gradually eroding the convective structure Sunday night into early 
next week. By the time Fausto moves into the vicinity of the 
Hawaiian Islands, it is forecast to be a weakening tropical storm 
with the deepest convection becoming increasingly displaced from the 
low-level center and the strongest winds confined to the northern 
side of the circulation. The NHC intensity forecast is little 
changed from the previous advisory and remains near the upper end of 
the guidance envelope.
 
Based on the predicted sheared nature of the storm, the risk of
sustained tropical-force-winds on land should be low as long as the
forecast track stays north of the islands. Interests in Hawaii
should continue to monitor the latest forecast updates.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Fausto is expected to weaken as it approaches the vicinity of the 
Hawaiian Islands early next week. Although confidence is increasing 
that the strongest winds and heaviest rainfall will remain offshore 
north of the islands, interests across Hawaii should continue to 
monitor the progress of Fausto.
 
2. Confidence is high that swells generated by Fausto will reach the
Hawaiian Islands well in advance of the cyclone, producing
increasing surf and dangerous rip currents. Surf is expected to
begin building across east-facing shores of the eastern end of the
state on Sunday, spreading westward Sunday night into Monday, and
continue building through Tuesday as Fausto approaches and moves
into the area.

----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...12.1N 106.7W
ABOUT 500 MI...810 KM SSW OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...80 MPH...130 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 295 DEGREES AT 15 MPH...24 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...987 MB...29.15 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM MST (0300 UTC), the center of Hurricane Genevieve was
located near latitude 12.1 North, longitude 106.7 West. Genevieve is
moving toward the west-northwest near 15 mph (24 km/h). A 
west-northwestward to northwestward motion with some decrease in 
forward speed is expected during the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 80 mph (130 km/h) 
with higher gusts.  Rapid intensification is expected during the 
next day or so, and Genevieve is forecast to become a major 
hurricane by late Sunday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 15 miles (30 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles
(205 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 987 mb (29.15 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF:  Swells generated by Genevieve are affecting portions of the
southwestern coast of Mexico and will likely reach southern portions
of the Baja California Peninsula Sunday night or Monday. These
swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions.  Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 AM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Berg

item.title: Hurricane Genevieve Forecast Discussion Number 7
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM MST Sat Jul 25 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 260235
TCDEP2
 
Hurricane Genevieve Discussion Number   7
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP072026
800 PM MST Sat Jul 25 2026
 
Inner-core convection continues to wrap around Genevieve's center,
while water vapor imagery shows well-established upper-level
outflow in nearly all quadrants of the storm. The Dvorak estimate
from TAFB is up to T4.0/65 kt, while the most recent UW-CIMSS ADT, 
AiDT, and DPRINT estimates are between 65 and 77 kt. Based on these 
data, Genevieve is upgraded to a 70-kt hurricane.
 
Genevieve continues to move west-northwestward (295 degrees) at 13
kt, steered by stronger-than-normal mid-tropospheric ridging that
extends from the southwestern United States down into the western
Caribbean Sea. This feature will continue to steer Genevieve
west-northwestward or northwestward for the next 5 days, although
the hurricane's speed may slow down to 7-8 kt in about 3 days when
a mid-level trough develops over southern Mexico. The track
guidance is very tightly clustered, and the new NHC track forecast
is nearly unchanged from the previous forecast.
 
Genevieve's strengthening hasn't reached a rapid rate quite yet,
but it might be on the verge of doing so. The hurricane will be
simultaneously experiencing a maximum of oceanic heat content and
upper-level divergence over the next 12 hours, along with generally
light shear. The consensus of SHIPS Rapid Intensification (RI)
guidance and DTOPS guidance is showing a 70-80 percent chance of a
30-kt increase over the next 24 hours, and a 55-80 percent chance
of a 45-kt increase over the next 36 hours. As a result, the NHC
intensity forecast continues to depict the occurrence of RI, with a
peak of 115 kt shown at 48 hours. This forecast still lies between
the latest HCCA and Google DeepMind ensemble mean solutions.
Gradual weakening is expected to begin by 60 hours due to a brief
increase in shear, cooler sea surface temperatures, and a drier and
more stable environment. That said, Genevieve is forecast to remain
a hurricane through day 5.
